facts.content: Patient presents with a sudden severe left-sided headache for 4 hours.
facts.source_text: CC: sudden severe L-sided headache ×4 h

facts.content: The headache had an abrupt onset.
The headache severity is reported as 6 out of 10.
The headache is associated with blurry vision with zig-zag lines.
The headache is associated with dizziness.
The headache worsens with movement.
The patient is unable to tolerate screens due to the headache.
The patient has vomited twice and has persistent nausea and vomiting.
The patient took paracetamol 3 hours ago without relief of the headache.
The patient denies limb weakness.
The patient denies gait change.
facts.source_text: Denies limb weakness or gait change

facts.content: Patient has a history of kidney stones.
Patient is on no regular medications.
The patient took paracetamol today.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's mother has migraines.
Patient's mother has hypothyroidism.
Patient denies being pregnant.
Review of systems is otherwise unremarkable.
Acute unilateral headache with visual aura, nausea, and vomiting is assessed as likely first-episode migraine.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute unilateral headache w/ visual aura, N/V ⟶ likely first-episode migraine

facts.content: Patient is assessed as having health anxiety regarding serious intracranial pathology.
facts.source_text: 2. Health anxiety re serious intracranial pathology

facts.content: Recommend ibuprofen and an over-the-counter antiemetic along with a sugary carbonated drink.
facts.source_text: • Recommend ibuprofen + OTC antiemetic; add sugary carbonated drink

facts.content: If there is inadequate relief, the patient should trial Migraleve or a similar triptan-containing agent.
facts.source_text: • If inadequate relief, trial Migraleve or similar triptan-containing agent

facts.content: Arrange a same-day in-person review for a full neurological examination.

facts.content: Advise emergency department attendance if there is sudden worsening, neurological deficit, vision loss, or intractable pain or vomiting.

facts.content: Reassure the patient and provide education on migraine course and red-flag symptoms.
